skill.name: wordpress-theme-development
skill.description: WordPress theme development workflow covering theme architecture, template hierarchy, custom post types, block editor support, responsive design, and WordPress 7.0 features: DataViews, Pattern Editing, Navigation Overlays, and admin refresh.
skill.summary: Build structured, responsive WordPress themes with block editor support and WordPress 7.0 guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All five static findings are false positives in documentation examples. The URLs are metadata or schema references, and the responsive grid text performs no reconnaissance.

finding_verdicts.reason: The URL is placeholder Theme URI metadata inside an example style.css header. It does not initiate a network request or transmit data.
The URL is placeholder Author URI metadata inside a documentation example. It is not executable and creates no network behavior.
This is the public GNU GPL license reference in an example theme header. It neither executes a request nor exposes information.
The URL identifies the official WordPress theme.json schema in a configuration example. It is declarative schema metadata, not data exfiltration or hidden network code.
The line only names a responsive grid block in a WordPress feature list. It contains no command, host inspection, environment query, or reconnaissance instruction.

content.value_statement: Building a complete WordPress theme requires coordinated templates, functions, block support, styling, and testing. This skill provides a phased workflow with practical examples and checklists.
actual_capabilities: Plans theme directories, core templates, theme headers, and function setup.
Explains template hierarchy for posts, pages, archives, search, and error pages.
Provides theme.json v3 settings and styles for block editor themes.
Guides custom post type, taxonomy, metadata, and REST API registration.
Covers block patterns, navigation overlays, breadcrumbs, and responsive styling.
Supplies accessibility, browser, performance, and WordPress compatibility checklists.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples, not a complete theme package.
WordPress 7.0 details require verification against the installed WordPress version.
Project-specific branding, content, plugins, hosting, and deployment requirements need separate input.
Generated themes still require security review, browser testing, accessibility testing, and performance validation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Starter Theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a WordPress theme for [site type]. List required files, template responsibilities, theme supports, menus, assets, and a practical implementation order.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Responsive Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this design specification into a WordPress theme plan: [design details]. Map layouts to templates, components, patterns, theme.json settings, and responsive breakpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Add Structured Content
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a custom post type for [content]. Include taxonomy, supported fields, sanitized REST-visible metadata, archive templates, editor behavior, and migration considerations.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Modernize a Theme
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this theme architecture: [details]. Identify template, block editor, accessibility, performance, and WordPress 7.0 gaps. Prioritize changes and define verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced maintainer planning a controlled modernization

output_examples.input: Plan a portfolio theme with projects, services, and a mobile navigation overlay.
output: Theme structure covering shared templates, project archives, service pages, patterns, assets, and translations.
Project content model with categories, sanitized client metadata, REST visibility, and archive behavior.
Responsive navigation plan with keyboard controls, accessible labels, and viewport testing.

output_examples.input: Review an existing theme before adding block editor support.
output: Compatibility assessment for templates, editor styles, theme settings, and registered supports.
Prioritized migration plan for theme.json, patterns, reusable styles, and editor testing.
Validation checklist covering content preservation, accessibility, responsive layouts, browsers, and performance.

output_examples.input: Define testing for a WordPress 7.0 theme upgrade.
output_examples.output: A focused test matrix covering templates, editor behavior, navigation overlays, patterns, custom content, accessibility, responsive breakpoints, browsers, and performance.

best_practices: Confirm the target WordPress and PHP versions before selecting APIs or features.
Sanitize stored metadata, escape rendered output, and use WordPress registration APIs.
Test templates, editor behavior, accessibility, responsiveness, browsers, and performance before release.
anti_patterns: Do not copy example identifiers, URLs, colors, or dimensions into production without review.
Do not place plugin-level business logic in a theme when content must survive theme changes.
Do not claim WordPress version compatibility without testing against that exact release.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete installable theme?
faq.answer: It provides a development workflow, examples, and checklists. A complete theme still requires project-specific implementation and validation.

faq.question: Does it support block themes?
faq.answer: It covers theme.json, block patterns, block registration, templates, and editor behavior. Adapt the workflow to classic, hybrid, or block architecture.

faq.question: Can it help create custom post types?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers registration, taxonomies, metadata, REST visibility, archive templates, and sanitization considerations.

faq.question: Is the WordPress 7.0 guidance guaranteed current?
faq.answer: No. Verify version-specific APIs and behavior against official documentation and the exact installed release.

faq.question: Does it replace security and accessibility review?
faq.answer: No. Use dedicated reviews and automated tests before deploying generated theme code.

faq.question: What project details should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the site type, content model, design system, target versions, required plugins, accessibility goals, performance targets, and deployment constraints.
